=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Location: _save_filed_records (line 548-551), _save_state (line 509-511)
  Issue: Both save helpers unconditionally call `log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`. For the v2 helper this is harmless because the dir already exists (we read from it earlier), but a parent-path deletion between load and save would silently re-create it under /root and write into the wrong location. The mkdir with parents=True can also create arbitrary intermediate directories if STATE_FILE ever resolves to a path whose parent is unexpectedly missing.
  Suggested minimal fix: drop the mkdir calls in _save_filed_records (we only just read from log_dir; if it disappeared mid-flight the write should fail loudly), or guard the mkdir with `if not log_dir.is_dir(): raise`. ~2 lines changed.
  estimated lines changed: 2
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2

- File: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Location: _migrate_legacy_counts (line 514-525) consumed by _load_filed_records (line 537)
  Issue: _load_filed_records parses filed-state.json with `json.loads(...).read_text(...)` first, then calls _load_state when "version" is missing. _load_state re-reads and re-parses the same file. For large legacy state files this is two reads + two JSON parses on every call. AD-4 documents this is accepted, but a defensive `if "version" not in raw_state: raw_state["version"] = 1; raw_state["filed"] = {sig: [] for sig in legacy_counts}` inline would avoid the second parse while preserving the migration semantics.
  Suggested minimal fix: inline the legacy state into the already-parsed dict instead of calling _load_state. Keep _load_state/_save_state intact (their signatures are §6-locked). ~4 lines added, 2 lines removed.
  estimated lines changed: 6
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

Note: I deliberately did not raise additional hardening suggestions for the regex itself. The "classifier error" branch is broader than outage-only and could swallow a real-block verdict whose reason happens to read "classifier error", but this is the explicit AD-5 design decision documented in the plan, not a defect introduced by the diff.
